items.name: bui
items.title: Beautiful UI primitives
items.description: Beautiful UI's primitives (MIT) as pikit's dashboard has them, fed by real data: the sidebar, the composer (its plus, slash and assistant menus), thinking, tool chips, context cards, pills, an operator's page, records tables, filter chips, a code block. They use the tokens and classes of the dashboard's src/index.css.

items.name: admin-proposals-settings
items.title: admin-proposals-settings
items.description: admin-proposals's section of the Settings dialog: The gate of the agent's changes to itself: its pull requests from pikit/self/* listed in the dashboard, with their diff and checks, approved (merged) or rejected there with a token the agent never holds; and the project's CI workflow. Dormant until connected, after deploying: the repository from the dashboard's Settings, the two tokens as secrets. Its settings come with the component (pikit add admin-proposals), stored by settings-store.

items.name: admin-proposals
items.title: admin-proposals
items.description: admin-proposals's view: The gate of the agent's changes to itself: its pull requests from pikit/self/* listed in the dashboard, with their diff and checks, approved (merged) or rejected there with a token the agent never holds; and the project's CI workflow. Dormant until connected, after deploying: the repository from the dashboard's Settings, the two tokens as secrets. Its admin API routes come with the component (pikit add admin-proposals).

items.name: agents-live-settings
items.title: agents-live-settings
items.description: agents-live's section of the Settings dialog: Agents as data: an operator creates, edits and removes agents (name, description, prompt, model, tools, extensions) in the dashboard's Settings, provided as agent.directory; with router-rules, routed to live. Its settings come with the component (pikit add agents-live), stored by settings-store.

items.name: github-app-settings
items.title: github-app-settings
items.description: github-app's section of the Settings dialog: Connects the project's GitHub repository in two clicks from the dashboard's Settings → GitHub: a GitHub App created in your account from a manifest and installed on the repository, whose short-lived installation tokens the app mints itself (`github`), its credentials sealed at rest. No token is pasted anywhere. Its settings come with the component (pikit add github-app), stored by settings-store.

items.name: github-token-settings
items.title: github-token-settings
items.description: github-token's section of the Settings dialog: The project's GitHub access (`github`) from a fine-grained token you made, the GITHUB_TOKEN secret, and the repository, a setting changed in the dashboard's Settings → GitHub: for a project run from the CLI or on a server. Its settings come with the component (pikit add github-token), stored by settings-store.

items.name: health-registry
items.title: health-registry
items.description: health-registry's view: What is up, degraded or down: components report their own state; /health fails when an essential one stays down, so the supervisor restarts the process. Its admin API routes come with the component (pikit add health-registry).

items.name: router-basic-settings
items.title: router-basic-settings
items.description: router-basic's section of the Settings dialog: Every message goes to one agent: `defaultAgent`. Its settings come with the component (pikit add router-basic), stored by settings-store.

items.name: router-rules-settings
items.title: router-rules-settings
items.description: router-rules's section of the Settings dialog: Each conversation goes to the agent of the first rule it matches: rules in config, edited live from the dashboard. Its settings come with the component (pikit add router-rules), stored by settings-store.
